newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends shade down on producer sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends shade down on producer sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended a shade down from New York's previous close after a quiet day with some producer selling, but traders ignored the U.S. Federal Reserve study advocating gold sales, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$340.60/341.10 on Monday compared to New York's previous close at US$340.80/341.30 on Friday.
"To be honest the (Federal Reserve) study drew very little interest indeed," said one trader.

Dealers said that most of Asia's gold activity was centered around currency movements, and with the dollar/yen and the Australian dollar trading on Monday in a narrow, stable band, gold had been quiet.
"It's just a bit of book squaring," said one dealer.
Others noted that enquiries had quickened after London opened, but that punters were interested in trading only small amounts.
"People are cautious and don't want big speculative positions," one source said.
Some dealers reported bits of physical gold sales,

The U.S. Federal Reserve on Friday issued a study arguing that government ownership of gold did not contribute directly to the general welfare and that the United States and other governments should sell off their gold reserves and reap huge benefits for their economies.
Local tael gold ended HK$3 down at HK$3,155
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -5.00 from its previous fix at -6.00.
